\chapter{Symbol Registry, Binding, and Precedence}
\chaptermark{Symbol Registry}
\label{sec:p01-symbol-registry}

The registry is normative for this handbook, not a claim that the literature
uses one notation.  Each row fixes a glyph, its formal or grammatical
standing, its scope, and (when it is an operator) its precedence.  Normally a
glyph receives another role only in a disjoint scope declared before use.  A
named primary calculus, logic, model, or method instead keeps its published
syntax: every overlapping local role must be typed and registered honestly,
not renamed to fit handbook notation.
\index{symbol registry}\index{notation!scope}

The editorial defaults are vertical bars for set cardinality,
\(\dom\mathcal M\) for a structure domain,
\(\mathcal M\equiv\mathcal N\) for elementary equivalence,
\(\varphi\Leftrightarrow\psi\) for formula equivalence,
\(\defeq\) for a definitional sign, and \(\forces\), with negation
\(\nforces\), for the declared forcing relation.  A source presentation's
explicitly typed local notation governs that presentation.  For example,
the inherited propositional semantics uses \(\varphi\equiv\psi\) for
equality of truth values under every valuation, whereas the displayed
structure operands in \(\mathcal M\equiv\mathcal N\) give the
elementary-equivalence role.  The register records both roles; neither
declaration renames the other presentation.

In the inherited CPL semantics the truth-value set is
\(\mathbb B=\{\mathbf F,\mathbf T\}\).

\begin{hbdefinition}{def:p02-uniform-substitution}{Substitution, uniform@Uniform substitution}
A \emph{uniform substitution}\index{formula instance} is a function
\(\upsilon:\mathsf{Prop}\to\mathsf{Fm}_{\mathsf{CPL}}\).  Its instance map is
defined recursively by
\[
 p_n[\upsilon]=\upsilon(p_n),\quad \bottom[\upsilon]=\bottom,\quad
 (\neg\varphi)[\upsilon]=\neg(\varphi[\upsilon]),\quad
 (\varphi\circ\psi)[\upsilon]=
   (\varphi[\upsilon]\circ\psi[\upsilon]).
\]
\end{hbdefinition}

\begin{lemma}[Substitution for open assumptions]
\label{lem:nd-substitution}
If \(D\) derives \(\psi\) with an open assumption \(\varphi\), and \(E\)
derives \(\varphi\), then replacing each designated open occurrence of
\(\varphi\) in \(D\) by a copy of \(E\), after consistently renaming every
label in every copy to be globally fresh from \(D\) and from all other copies,
produces a derivation of \(\psi\).  Its open assumptions are those of \(D\)
other than the replaced occurrences, together with the correspondingly
renamed open assumptions of the inserted copies of \(E\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Substitution lemma]
\label{thm:fol-substitution}
For every formula \(\varphi\), term \(t\), variable \(x\), structure
\(\Meta\), and assignment \(s\),
\[
 \Meta,s\entails\varphi[t/x]
 \quad\text{iff}\quad
 \Meta,s[x\mapsto\sem{t}^{\Meta}_s]\entails\varphi.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{hbdefinition}{def:p10-modal-lindenbaum}{The normal modal Lindenbaum algebra}
Put
\[
 \varphi\equiv_L\psi
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
       \vdash_L\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi.
\]
The following theorem verifies that this is a congruence.
Let \(F_L\) be the quotient of the formula algebra by this relation,
with classes \([\varphi]_L\) and induced operations
\[
\begin{gathered}
 0=[\bot]_L,\quad 1=[\top]_L,\quad
 \neg[\varphi]_L=[\neg\varphi]_L,\\
 [\varphi]_L\wedge[\psi]_L=[\varphi\wedge\psi]_L,\qquad
 \Box[\varphi]_L=[\Box\varphi]_L.
\end{gathered}
\]
This is the \emph{normal modal Lindenbaum algebra} of \(L\).
\index{Lindenbaum--Tarski algebra!normal modal logic}
\end{hbdefinition}

\begin{annexitem}{annex:p10.modal-algebra.1}{thm:p10-modal-algebra-completeness}{The modal quotient and algebraic completeness}
\begin{proof}
Classical propositional reasoning makes \(\equiv_L\) an
equivalence relation compatible with all Boolean connectives.
For the modal constructor, if
\(\vdash_L\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi\), then both implications
are theorems.  Necessitate each and apply distribution to obtain
\[
 \vdash_L\Box\varphi\to\Box\psi,\qquad
 \vdash_L\Box\psi\to\Box\varphi.
\]
Their conjunction yields
\(\vdash_L\Box\varphi\leftrightarrow\Box\psi\).
The quotient operations are therefore well-defined.
Boolean identities hold because their formula counterparts are
propositional tautologies.

The formula \(\Box\top\) is a theorem by necessitation.
Necessitating the two projections of a conjunction and applying
distribution proves
\(\Box(\varphi\wedge\psi)\to
(\Box\varphi\wedge\Box\psi)\).
For the converse, necessitate
\(\varphi\to(\psi\to\varphi\wedge\psi)\) and apply
distribution twice.
Thus \(\Box\) preserves \(1\) and binary meets in \(F_L\).
Taking Boolean duals shows that \(\Diamond\) preserves
\(0\) and binary joins.
This proves that \(F_L\) is a normal modal algebra.

Classical tautologies also give
\[
 [\chi]_L=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\chi\in L:
\]
each of \(\chi\) and \(\chi\leftrightarrow\top\) implies
the other by propositional reasoning.
Induction on formulas gives
\[
 \llbracket\chi\rrbracket_\nu^{F_L}=[\chi]_L,
 \qquad \nu(p)=[p]_L.
\]

\paragraph{All valuations in the quotient.}
Fix \(\lambda\in L\) and an arbitrary valuation
\(v:\mathsf{Prop}\to F_L\).
Only finitely many variables occur in \(\lambda\).
For each of those variables \(p\), select a formula \(\rho_p\)
with \([\rho_p]_L=v(p)\).
Define a substitution \(\sigma\) by these finitely many choices,
and put \(\sigma(q)=q\) on all other variables.
Induction on the subformulas of \(\lambda\) gives
\[
 \llbracket\lambda\rrbracket_v^{F_L}=[\sigma(\lambda)]_L.
\]
Uniform-substitution closure puts \(\sigma(\lambda)\) in \(L\),
so this value is \(1\).
This proves \(F_L\in\operatorname{Alg}(L)\).
There was no selection of representatives for a whole infinite
family of equivalence classes.

If \(\varphi\notin L\), its value under \(\nu\) is not \(1\),
so \(F_L\) refutes it.  Conversely, every member of \(L\)
is valid in every member of \(\operatorname{Alg}(L)\) by
definition.  These statements prove all displayed equivalences.

The algebra definition also respects the stated normal-logic rules.
Meet preservation makes \(\Box_A\) monotone, and
\[
 \Box_A(a\to b)\wedge\Box_Aa
       =\Box_A((a\to b)\wedge a)\leq\Box_Ab
\]
proves distribution.
Modus ponens preserves validity, substitution is composition
with formula evaluation, and theorem necessitation preserves
validity because \(\Box_A1=1\).
Thus, if \(L\) is presented by additional axioms, validating
those axioms in a normal modal algebra validates every theorem.

If \(\bot\in L\), propositional explosion gives every formula
in \(L\); hence every two formulas are equivalent and \(F_L\)
is trivial.  Conversely, a trivial quotient has
\([\bot]_L=1\), so \(L\) is inconsistent.
Any algebra validating this logic must have \(0=1\);
the trivial modal algebras do validate every formula.
\end{proof}
\end{annexitem}

\section{Valuations and recursive truth clauses}
\label{sec:prop-syntax-semantics-02}

\begin{definition}[Truth values and valuation]
Let \(\B\defeq\set{\False,\True}\).  A \emph{valuation} is a function
\(v:\Prop\to\B\).  Its unique extension
\(\widehat v:\Fm_{\CPL}\to\B\) is defined by structural recursion:
\[
\begin{array}{rcl}
\widehat v(p_n)&=&v(p_n),\\
\widehat v(\bottom)&=&\False,\\
\widehat v(\neg\varphi)&=&\True
  \quad\text{iff}\quad\widehat v(\varphi)=\False,\\
\widehat v(\varphi\land\psi)&=&\True
  \quad\text{iff}\quad
  \widehat v(\varphi)=\True\text{ and }\widehat v(\psi)=\True,\\
\widehat v(\varphi\lor\psi)&=&\True
  \quad\text{iff}\quad
  \widehat v(\varphi)=\True\text{ or }\widehat v(\psi)=\True,\\
\widehat v(\varphi\to\psi)&=&\False
  \quad\text{iff}\quad
  \widehat v(\varphi)=\True\text{ and }\widehat v(\psi)=\False.
\end{array}
\]
We write \(v\entails\varphi\) iff
\(\widehat v(\varphi)=\True\).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Coincidence for propositional formulas]
\label{lem:prop-coincidence}
If valuations \(v\) and \(w\) agree on every propositional variable occurring
in \(\varphi\), then
\(\widehat v(\varphi)=\widehat w(\varphi)\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Proceed by structural induction on \(\varphi\).  The variable case is the
hypothesis, and the \(\bottom\) case is immediate.  Each connective case
follows by applying the induction hypotheses to the immediate subformulas and
then applying the corresponding recursive truth clause.
\end{proof}

\begin{hbdefinition}{def:p02-uniform-substitution}{Substitution, uniform@Uniform substitution}
A \emph{uniform substitution}\index{formula instance} is a function
\(\upsilon:\mathsf{Prop}\to\mathsf{Fm}_{\mathsf{CPL}}\).  Its instance map is
defined recursively by
\[
 p_n[\upsilon]=\upsilon(p_n),\quad \bottom[\upsilon]=\bottom,\quad
 (\neg\varphi)[\upsilon]=\neg(\varphi[\upsilon]),\quad
 (\varphi\circ\psi)[\upsilon]=
   (\varphi[\upsilon]\circ\psi[\upsilon]).
\]
\end{hbdefinition}

\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p02-uniform-substitution}{cited=Kleene1952}{Uniform-substitution theorem}
For every uniform substitution \(\upsilon\): if \(\entails\varphi\), then
\(\entails\varphi[\upsilon]\); and if
\(\varphi\Leftrightarrow\psi\), then
\(\varphi[\upsilon]\Leftrightarrow\psi[\upsilon]\).
\end{hbtheorem}

\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p02-replacement}{cited=Kleene1952}{Replacement theorem}
Logical equivalence is an equivalence relation and a congruence for each
primitive connective.  Hence, if \(\psi\Leftrightarrow\chi\) and
\(\varphi'\) results from \(\varphi\) by replacing any chosen occurrences
of the subformula \(\psi\) by \(\chi\), then
\(\varphi\Leftrightarrow\varphi'\).
\end{hbtheorem}

The preceding two statements fill depth row D-P2-010.  They distinguish
uniform substitution for variables from replacement at selected subformula
occurrences.

\begin{lemma}[Substitution for open assumptions]
\label{lem:nd-substitution}
If \(D\) derives \(\psi\) with an open assumption \(\varphi\), and \(E\)
derives \(\varphi\), then replacing each designated open occurrence of
\(\varphi\) in \(D\) by a copy of \(E\), after consistently renaming every
label in every copy to be globally fresh from \(D\) and from all other copies,
produces a derivation of \(\psi\).  Its open assumptions are those of \(D\)
other than the replaced occurrences, together with the correspondingly
renamed open assumptions of the inserted copies of \(E\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
First reserve for each designated occurrence a set of labels disjoint from
the labels of \(D\) and from the sets reserved for the other occurrences, and
consistently rename its copy of \(E\) into that set.  Strengthen the induction
invariant by requiring every inserted copy to use its reserved globally fresh
labels.  Induct on the height of \(D\).  If \(D\) is the designated
assumption, use its renamed copy of \(E\).  If it is another assumption, leave
it unchanged.  For an inference, apply the induction hypothesis to each
immediate subderivation and then reapply the same rule with the original
discharge labels of \(D\).  Consistent renaming preserves every discharge
internal to a copy of \(E\), while global freshness makes every label of that
copy different from every label on a rule of \(D\).  Hence no rule above a
graft point can accidentally discharge an open assumption of the inserted
copy, and the stated open-assumption accounting follows.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Substitution lemma]
\label{thm:fol-substitution}
For every formula \(\varphi\), term \(t\), variable \(x\), structure
\(\Meta\), and assignment \(s\),
\[
 \Meta,s\entails\varphi[t/x]
 \quad\text{iff}\quad
 \Meta,s[x\mapsto\sem{t}^{\Meta}_s]\entails\varphi.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Proceed by induction on formula complexity.  Atomic cases follow from
\cref{lem:term-substitution}.  Connective cases follow immediately from the
induction hypotheses.

Let \(\varphi=Qy\,\psi\), where
\(Q\in\set{\forall,\exists}\).  If \(y=x\), substitution stops at the
quantifier.  Updating \(x\) before evaluating \(Qx\,\psi\) is immaterial,
because the quantified update of \(x\) overrides it.  If \(y\ne x\) and
\(y\notin\operatorname{Var}(t)\), then
\(\sem{t}^{\Meta}_{s[y\mapsto a]}=\sem{t}^{\Meta}_s\) for every \(a\).
Apply the induction hypothesis to \(\psi\) under each updated assignment and
then apply the truth clause for \(Q\).

If \(y\ne x\) and \(y\in\operatorname{Var}(t)\), the definition first replaces \(y\) by a
fresh \(z\).  The variable \(z\) occurs neither in \(t\) nor free in
\(\psi\).  The induction hypothesis applied to the renamed body---
legitimate because renaming preserves complexity, by
\cref{lem:substitution-complexity}---together with formula coincidence,
shows directly that
\(Qy\,\psi\) and \(Qz\,(\psi[z/y])\) have the same satisfaction condition.
The preceding quantifier argument then applies to the renamed body, whose
complexity equals \(c(\psi)\) by \cref{lem:substitution-complexity}.  Thus
the equivalence holds in all cases.
\end{proof}

\begin{hbdefinition}{def:p10-modal-lindenbaum}{The normal modal Lindenbaum algebra}
Put
\[
 \varphi\equiv_L\psi
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
       \vdash_L\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi.
\]
The following theorem verifies that this is a congruence.
Let \(F_L\) be the quotient of the formula algebra by this relation,
with classes \([\varphi]_L\) and induced operations
\[
\begin{gathered}
 0=[\bot]_L,\quad 1=[\top]_L,\quad
 \neg[\varphi]_L=[\neg\varphi]_L,\\
 [\varphi]_L\wedge[\psi]_L=[\varphi\wedge\psi]_L,\qquad
 \Box[\varphi]_L=[\Box\varphi]_L.
\end{gathered}
\]
This is the \emph{normal modal Lindenbaum algebra} of \(L\).
\index{Lindenbaum--Tarski algebra!normal modal logic}
\end{hbdefinition}

 \operatorname{Alg}(L)\models\varphi.
\]

\begin{proof}
Classical propositional reasoning makes \(\equiv_L\) an
equivalence relation compatible with all Boolean connectives.
For the modal constructor, if
\(\vdash_L\varphi\leftrightarrow\psi\), then both implications
are theorems.  Necessitate each and apply distribution to obtain
\[
 \vdash_L\Box\varphi\to\Box\psi,\qquad
 \vdash_L\Box\psi\to\Box\varphi.
\]
Their conjunction yields
\(\vdash_L\Box\varphi\leftrightarrow\Box\psi\).
The quotient operations are therefore well-defined.
Boolean identities hold because their formula counterparts are
propositional tautologies.

\begin{hbtheorem}{thm:p02-equality-laws}{proved=annex:p2.fol.calc.4}{Derived equality laws}
For all \(\mathcal L\)-terms \(r,t,u\), every formula \(\varphi\), and every
variable \(x\), the natural-deduction equality rules on
\hyperref[sheet:nd-fol]{\texttt{sheet:nd-fol}} derive:
\[
 \varnothing\derives_{\mathsf{ND}_{\mathsf{FOL}}}t=t,
 \qquad
 \{r=t\}\derives_{\mathsf{ND}_{\mathsf{FOL}}}t=r,
\]
\[
 \{r=t,t=u\}\derives_{\mathsf{ND}_{\mathsf{FOL}}}r=u,
 \qquad
 \{r=t,\varphi[r/x]\}
   \derives_{\mathsf{ND}_{\mathsf{FOL}}}\varphi[t/x].
\]
Every displayed substitution is the total capture-avoiding operation of the
syntax chapter.  Reflexivity and replacement are the registered primitive
rules; symmetry and transitivity are derived, not silently added axioms.
\end{hbtheorem}
